text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursdsay. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Parliament's foreign affairs committee backed the holding of a no-confidence vote against Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs, attacking him for poor relations with Russia and unsolved issues with neighbours Lithuania and Estonia. Most politicians believe the vote will fail.

- The three Baltic presidents will meet in Riga on November 26 and are expected to discuss the border issues and sign a joint declaration. There was speculation that Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas may not attend the talks after a reported insult against his staff by Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele but this has not been confirmed.
- Latvia has sent to Bosnia humanitarian relief worth of 50,000 lats.
- Shkele is to propose amendments to the recently adopted law on local elections to allow people who were members of the Communist Party after January 13, 1991 to be allowed to run in elections.

- The preparation of a new law on the status of refugees and asylum seekers in Latvia is close to completion and will next week be submitted to the cabinet. The law is expected to take effect at the start of next year and will be backed financially by the U.N. and Sweden.
- The EBRD signed a deal to buy 23 percent of Riga Commercial Bank for 2.67 million lats.
